title: Fasten a GoPro into a helmet's buckle: line up the five fingers' holes, push the thumb screw through and run it down
instruction: Fasten the GoPro to the helmet's mount with its thumb screw, facing forward and level.
context: Anyone who puts an action camera on a helmet, handlebar or chest mount does this, and GoPro alone sold about 3 million cameras in 2023. The camera's two fingers must be held between the buckle's three with all five holes lined up within about a millimetre while the other hand pushes the screw through; hold the camera a little low or let go and the screw stops on its first finger. Then the camera has to be held level while the screw is turned home, or it flops over on the loose screw.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights above the table. Helmet: a yellow HDPE hard hat (NVIDIA SimReady ppe_helmet_hardHat_a01, 29.0 x 20.8 x 17.3 cm), taped to the table, centred at (30, 0), brim towards +x; crown 17.35 cm up. On its crown at (30, 0): a GoPro curved adhesive mount (black plastic base 4.2 x 4.0 x 0.4 cm with a 1.2 mm foam adhesive pad) with a GoPro mounting buckle clipped in (body 2.6 x 2.4 x 0.8 cm). The buckle's three fingers: 3.0 mm thick, 3.3 mm gaps, 12 mm wide, rounded (6 mm radius) about 5.2 mm holes whose axis runs along y, 2.0 cm above the crown; the slots' floor is 8 mm below the axis. The left outer finger holds an M5 steel hex nut (8 mm across flats, 4 mm thick) in a hex boss on its outside. Thumb screw: M5 x 0.8 steel thread 20 mm long under a black plastic neck (9 mm across, 22 mm long) and a flat paddle head (18 x 12 x 6 mm), 54 mm in all, about 7 g; backed out with its tip 0.15 mm inside the right outer finger's hole (the head's shoulder 17.15 mm from that finger), paddle lying flat, 4.7 to 5.9 cm right of the buckle's centre. Camera: GoPro HERO (2024), black, 56.6 wide x 47.7 high x 29.4 deep mm, 86 g, its two folding mounting fingers folded out (3.0 mm thick, 3.3 mm apart, 12 mm wide, 5.2 mm holes 10 mm below the body); lying on its right side, lens towards +x, top towards -y, fingers pointing +y, the fingers' hole axis at (24, 20), 2.83 cm up. Distractors (SimReady, loose): sunglasses (accessory_eyeglasses_a01, 14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, 30 g) at (50, 24), turned 90 degrees; a bottle of drink (food_beverage_bottledDrink_a01, 5.3 cm across, 17.5 cm tall, 550 g) at (47, -24); a pair of cloth work gloves (ppe_gloves_cloth_a01, 23.3 x 25.2 x 5.3 cm, 120 g) at (58, -2). Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read at the end, before anyone touches the scene. Standoff: the gap between the shoulder under the screw's head and the buckle's right outer finger (ruler or feeler gauge: 17.15 mm at the start, 3.2 mm when the tip reaches the nut, 0 when run down). 0 unless the screw passes through both of the camera's fingers (both camera-finger holes within 1 mm of the screw's axis, standoff 7.0 mm or less) and every fingertip point of both grippers (each finger's tip and 3 cm up it, middle and both edges) is at least 3 cm from the camera, the screw and the buckle. Then 0.25; 0.5 with the standoff 3.0 mm or less (threaded at least a quarter turn into the nut); 0.75 with it 0.5 mm or less (run down); 1.0 when, run down, the lens points forward within 5 degrees of the helmet's front-to-back line, held for 2 s with the grippers clear and the camera still (it moves less than 1 mm and 0.5 degrees in those 2 s); the trial ends there. Anything else scores 0, including the camera on the table, an empty buckle with the screw run down, and a gripper still on the camera.
reset_notes: Hold the camera, unscrew the thumb screw and draw it back until its shoulder is 17 mm from the outer finger (tip just inside that finger's hole), lift the camera out and lay it on its tape marks; put the distractors back on theirs. Nothing is consumed; check the buckle's fingers for cracks every 20 trials.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX, 240 Hz). Camera, buckle and screw are authored meshes at real size (SimReady has no GoPro); the helmet (a hard hat) and distractors are SimReady. Finger and screw contacts are real (each hole is 16 convex pieces, 0.15 mm clearance). The thread is code: once the tip reaches the nut, axial travel follows the turn, 0.8 mm per turn; at the seat the turn is held and the outer fingers clamp 25 N. Uniform friction; no thread torque, no screw droop.
